blogPosts.title: How Much Does Concrete Resurfacing Cost in Geelong? (2026 Guide)
blogPosts.excerpt: Discover the real cost of concrete resurfacing in Geelong, South Geelong, and the Bellarine Peninsula, including pricing factors, material options, and tips to get the best value in 2026.
body: If you are a Geelong homeowner wondering about the cost of concrete resurfacing, you are not alone. Across South Geelong, Belmont, and Highton, more and more property owners are choosing resurfacing over full replacement as a cost-effective way to revive tired driveways, paths, and patios. In 2026, concrete resurfacing in the Geelong region typically costs between $30 and $60 per square metre, depending on the condition of the existing surface, the type of finish selected, and the complexity of the job. Factors like access, colour choice, and whether decorative elements are required will all influence your final price. Here is what you need to know before getting a quote from a South Geelong concreting specialist.

The first major factor affecting the cost of concrete resurfacing in Geelong is the condition of your existing concrete. If your surface is structurally sound with only minor cosmetic issues such as fading, light staining, or surface wear, the preparation work is minimal and costs stay on the lower end of the scale. However, if there are significant cracks, uneven sections, or areas where the concrete has lifted due to Geelong's reactive clay soils — particularly common in newer estates around Armstrong Creek and Waurn Ponds — additional repair work will be needed before resurfacing can begin. A thorough on-site assessment by a qualified South Geelong concreter will identify exactly what preparation is required and give you an accurate, fixed price for the entire project.

The type of resurfacing system you choose will also impact pricing considerably. Polymer-modified cementitious coatings are the most common and affordable option, typically ranging from $30 to $45 per square metre in the Geelong area. These coatings bond directly to the existing concrete and can be finished in a wide range of colours and textures. Spray on paving systems, which Bay City Spray on Paving specialises in, fall in a similar price range but offer superior UV resistance and durability — an important consideration for exposed Bellarine Peninsula properties in Ocean Grove, Point Lonsdale, and Queenscliff where salt air and strong sunlight accelerate surface degradation significantly.

For homeowners in south west Melbourne suburbs like Werribee, Point Cook, and Hoppers Crossing, the cost of concrete resurfacing is broadly comparable to Geelong pricing, though travel charges may apply depending on the project size. In most cases, a standard driveway resurfacing in the greater Geelong region will cost between $1,500 and $3,500 for a typical residential driveway of 40 to 60 square metres. Larger commercial projects in Corio or Lara will be priced on a per-square-metre basis, with volume discounts often available for bigger areas. Always ensure your quote includes surface preparation, material costs, labour, and cleanup — a reputable South Geelong concreter like Bay City provides fully inclusive, fixed-price quotes with no hidden extras.

One of the biggest advantages of resurfacing over full replacement is the significant time savings. A complete driveway replacement in Geelong can take five to seven days including demolition, ground preparation, and concrete curing, while a resurfacing project typically takes just one to two days. This means less disruption to your household and lower overall costs. For Geelong families who use their driveway daily, this is a substantial benefit. Additionally, resurfacing is far more environmentally friendly than full replacement, as it avoids sending hundreds of kilograms of old concrete to landfill. If sustainability matters to you and your family, resurfacing is the clear winner for your South Geelong property.

When budgeting for your Geelong concrete resurfacing project, it is worth considering the long-term value rather than just the upfront cost. A quality resurfacing job with premium materials should last 10 to 15 years or more with basic maintenance, compared to just three to five years for cheap paint-based products that peel and flake under Geelong's harsh conditions. In Geelong's coastal climate, where surfaces are exposed to salt air, intense UV, and occasional heavy rainfall, investing in a professional-grade system pays for itself many times over. Contact Bay City Spray on Paving for a free, no-obligation assessment at your South Geelong or greater Geelong property today.

blogPosts.title: Spray on Paving vs Traditional Paving: Which Is Better for Geelong Homes?
blogPosts.excerpt: A comprehensive comparison of spray on paving and traditional paving for Geelong properties, covering durability, cost, maintenance, and suitability for coastal conditions.
body: When it comes to upgrading your outdoor surfaces in Geelong, the choice between spray on paving and traditional paving can be confusing for homeowners. Both options are popular across the Bellarine Peninsula and greater Geelong region, but they serve different purposes, have different costs, and offer distinct advantages depending on your property type and climate exposure. This comprehensive guide breaks down the key differences between spray on paving and traditional paving for Geelong homeowners, covering everything from initial cost and installation time to long-term durability and maintenance requirements. Whether you are in South Geelong, Ocean Grove, or Point Cook, understanding these differences will help you make the right investment for your property.

Traditional paving involves laying individual pavers — typically concrete, clay, or natural stone — over a prepared base of compacted road base and sand. In the Geelong region, traditional paver driveways generally cost between $60 and $120 per square metre installed, with premium natural stone options like bluestone or granite reaching $150 or more. The installation process is labour-intensive, requiring careful ground preparation, precise levelling, and jointing between each paver. In contrast, spray on paving is applied as a liquid system directly over an existing concrete substrate or newly poured slab, typically costing between $30 and $55 per square metre. For Geelong homeowners on a budget, spray on paving offers a significant cost saving without sacrificing appearance or durability.

Durability is a critical consideration in Geelong's coastal environment, and this is where the two systems differ significantly. Traditional pavers can shift, sink, and become uneven over time, particularly in areas with reactive clay soils — a common issue in suburbs like Waurn Ponds, Armstrong Creek, and Lara where the ground expands and contracts with moisture changes. Once pavers shift, they create trip hazards and allow weed growth in the joints. Spray on paving, by contrast, creates a seamless, monolithic surface with no joints for weeds to penetrate. The polymer-modified system bonds directly to the concrete substrate, moving with it rather than against it, which makes it far more resilient to ground movement across the Geelong region.

Maintenance requirements differ substantially between the two options and this is a major factor for busy Geelong families. Traditional paver driveways in Geelong require regular re-sanding of joints, occasional individual paver replacement, and periodic pressure cleaning to prevent moss and algae buildup — a particular concern in the damp Bellarine Peninsula climate around Drysdale, St Leonards, and Indented Heads. Spray on paving requires only basic cleaning with a broom or hose and an occasional pressure wash to maintain its appearance. For busy Geelong families and property managers overseeing multiple properties across the region, the low-maintenance nature of spray on paving is a compelling advantage that saves both time and money year after year.

Aesthetic options are another important factor for Geelong homeowners to consider. Traditional paving offers a classic, textured look with a wide range of paver styles, from traditional red brick to modern large-format concrete pavers. Spray on paving provides equally impressive visual options, including exposed aggregate effects, stone-look finishes, and custom colour matching to complement your home's exterior. For South Geelong homes with heritage character, spray on paving can replicate traditional looks without the maintenance headaches of individual pavers. For modern builds in newer Geelong estates around Armstrong Creek and Charlemont, both systems offer contemporary finishes that enhance curb appeal and property value in the current market.

Installation time is another practical difference that matters for Geelong homeowners and businesses. A traditional paver driveway for a typical Geelong home takes three to five days to complete, including ground preparation, laying, and jointing. A spray on paving project of the same area can often be completed in one to two days, meaning far less disruption to your daily routine. For Geelong commercial properties like car parks and retail forecourts, this faster turnaround translates directly to less business disruption and lost revenue. If you are considering upgrading your outdoor surfaces in Geelong, the Bellarine Peninsula, or south west Melbourne, contact Bay City Spray on Paving to discuss which system best suits your property, budget, and lifestyle requirements.

blogPosts.title: The Best Time to Pour Concrete in Geelong and Victoria's Southwest
blogPosts.excerpt: Learn the ideal seasons and weather conditions for pouring concrete in Geelong, the Bellarine Peninsula, and south west Melbourne to avoid cracking and ensure longevity.
body: Pouring concrete in Geelong requires careful timing to account for the region's variable coastal climate. Whether you are building a new driveway in South Geelong, laying a slab in Belmont, or constructing a commercial foundation in Corio, the weather conditions at the time of pouring will directly affect the quality, strength, and longevity of your finished concrete. Geelong sits in a temperate oceanic climate zone with mild summers, cool winters, and relatively consistent rainfall throughout the year — but the timing of your pour within these seasons makes a significant difference to the outcome. Understanding the best conditions for pouring concrete in the Geelong region will save you money, prevent costly repairs, and ensure your investment lasts for decades.

The ideal time to pour concrete in Geelong and the Bellarine Peninsula is during the mild autumn and spring months, from March to May and September to November. During these periods, daytime temperatures typically range from 15 to 25 degrees Celsius, providing optimal conditions for concrete to cure evenly without excessive moisture loss or thermal stress. The moderate humidity levels in Geelong during these months also help prevent the concrete surface from drying too quickly, which is one of the leading causes of surface cracking. Many experienced concreters in the Geelong area, including Bay City Spray on Paving, schedule the majority of their new pour work during these shoulder seasons to take advantage of these favourable conditions for their clients.

Summer pours in Geelong require additional precautions but are certainly manageable with proper planning and local expertise. December, January, and February can bring temperatures above 35 degrees, particularly during hot north-westerly winds that occasionally sweep across the Bellarine Peninsula from the Victorian interior. When pouring concrete in Geelong during summer, it is essential to start early in the morning — before 7am is ideal — to allow the concrete to begin setting before the peak heat of the day. Wet curing methods, such as applying curing compounds or covering the fresh concrete with wet hessian, become critical in these conditions to prevent rapid moisture evaporation and plastic shrinkage cracking, which is a common issue across south west Melbourne and the Geelong region in summer months.

Winter concrete pours in Geelong present different but equally manageable challenges. From June through August, overnight temperatures can drop below five degrees, and morning frosts are common in inland suburbs like Lara, Corio, and Waurn Ponds. Concrete should not be poured when temperatures are forecast to fall below five degrees within the first 24 hours of curing, as this can prevent proper hydration and significantly reduce the concrete's final strength. Geelong's proximity to Bass Strait does moderate winter temperatures compared to inland areas, but caution is still required for every project. If a winter pour is unavoidable — as sometimes happens with commercial construction timelines in the Geelong area — accelerators, insulated blankets, and heated enclosures can be used to maintain adequate curing temperatures throughout the critical early hours.

Geelong's unique geography also plays a role in concrete pouring conditions that many builders overlook. Properties closer to the coast, in suburbs like Ocean Grove, Point Lonsdale, Queenscliff, and Barwon Heads, experience higher humidity, salt-laden air, and more consistent temperatures than properties further inland. While the humidity is generally beneficial for concrete curing, the salt content in the air can affect surface finishes if not properly accounted for — particularly for exposed aggregate and decorative concrete work. Inland Geelong suburbs like Highton, Belmont, and Drysdale tend to experience wider temperature fluctuations and lower humidity, making moisture management during curing more critical. An experienced local concreter understands these microclimatic differences and adjusts their techniques accordingly for every project.

Planning your concrete project in Geelong? The best approach is to book your pour well in advance with a reputable local concreter who understands the region's climate patterns and seasonal variations. At Bay City Spray on Paving, we monitor weather forecasts closely and will advise on the optimal pour date for your specific project and location across the Geelong region. Whether you are in South Geelong, the Bellarine Peninsula, or south west Melbourne, we ensure every pour is completed under the right conditions for maximum durability and strength. Contact us for a free on-site assessment and we will help you plan your project for the ideal time of year, ensuring your concrete investment stands the test of Geelong's coastal climate for decades to come.

blogPosts.title: Exposed Aggregate Driveways in South Geelong: Costs, Process & Benefits
blogPosts.excerpt: Everything you need to know about exposed aggregate driveways in South Geelong, from the pouring process and costs to why they are the top choice for Geelong homeowners.
body: Exposed aggregate concrete has become one of the most popular driveway choices for homeowners in South Geelong and across the greater Geelong region, and for excellent reasons. This versatile finish combines the structural strength of reinforced concrete with the natural beauty of exposed stone aggregate, creating a driveway surface that is both visually striking and incredibly durable. In 2026, exposed aggregate driveways in South Geelong typically cost between $80 and $150 per square metre installed, depending on the type of aggregate selected, the size of the driveway, and site-specific factors such as access and ground conditions. For a standard residential driveway of 50 square metres, expect to invest between $4,000 and $7,500 — a price point that delivers outstanding long-term value for Geelong homeowners.

The process of creating an exposed aggregate driveway begins with careful planning and meticulous site preparation. In the Geelong region, where reactive clay soils are common in suburbs like Waurn Ponds, Armstrong Creek, and Lara, proper ground preparation is essential to prevent future cracking and settlement. This typically involves excavating to a depth of 150 to 200 millimetres, installing a compacted road base, and laying a moisture barrier before the steel reinforcement and concrete are placed. The concrete is poured to a minimum thickness of 100 millimetres — often 125 millimetres for driveways bearing regular vehicle traffic — and the selected aggregate is broadcast evenly onto the wet surface. After initial setting, the surface paste is carefully removed with a specialised washing and brushing technique to reveal the beautiful stone beneath.

One of the key advantages of exposed aggregate for Geelong driveways is its exceptional slip resistance in all weather conditions. The textured surface created by the protruding aggregate stones provides natural grip even when wet, making it an ideal choice for the Bellarine Peninsula and coastal Geelong suburbs where morning dew and sea mist can make smooth surfaces treacherous for pedestrians. This slip-resistant quality makes exposed aggregate equally popular for pool surrounds, paths, and entertainment areas throughout Geelong and the surrounding regions. Unlike plain concrete, which can become dangerously slick when wet, exposed aggregate maintains reliable traction year-round. For families in South Geelong with children playing in the driveway, this safety benefit alone often justifies the modest additional cost over standard plain concrete finishes.

The selection of aggregate stone significantly affects both the appearance and cost of your finished driveway and this is where personal preference plays a major role. Popular choices among Geelong homeowners include locally sourced river pebbles in warm earth tones, crushed granite in greys and whites, and premium quartz aggregates that sparkle beautifully in sunlight. In coastal suburbs like Ocean Grove and Point Lonsdale, lighter-coloured aggregates that reflect heat are particularly popular, keeping the driveway surface cooler during Geelong's increasingly hot summer days. The colour and size of the aggregate, combined with the base concrete colour, create virtually unlimited design possibilities for your property. At Bay City Spray on Paving, we carry a wide range of aggregate samples at our South Geelong location so you can see and feel the options before making your final selection for your driveway project.

Maintaining an exposed aggregate driveway in Geelong is straightforward but important for long-term preservation of your investment. The sealed surface should be resealed every two to three years to protect against staining and weather erosion — particularly important for properties in Geelong's coastal suburbs where salt air accelerates surface degradation over time. Regular sweeping and occasional pressure washing with a low-pressure setting will keep the aggregate looking fresh and vibrant for many years. Avoid using harsh chemical cleaners or high-pressure washers directly on the aggregate surface, as these can dislodge individual stones and cause damage. For Geelong property owners, the minimal maintenance requirements of exposed aggregate make it one of the most practical driveway options available, combining genuine beauty with everyday durability that stands up to Australian conditions.

If you are considering an exposed aggregate driveway for your South Geelong property, choosing the right concreter is just as important as choosing the right aggregate stone. The quality of the finish depends entirely on the skill and experience of the installer — the timing of the wash-off, the depth of exposure, and the consistency of the finish across the entire surface all require expertise that comes only with years of practice in the Geelong region. Bay City Spray on Paving has been pouring exposed aggregate driveways across Geelong, the Bellarine Peninsula, and south west Melbourne for years, and our portfolio of completed projects speaks for itself. Contact us for a free on-site consultation at your South Geelong property and discover how an exposed aggregate driveway can transform your home's curb appeal and long-term value.
